newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cavallo warns Brazil against Argentine errors.
newsitem.headline: Cavallo warns Brazil against Argentine errors.

text.p: Former Argentine economy minister Domingo warned Brazil against repeating mistakes made by Buenos Aires that have left Argentina with low inflation but 17.1 percent unemployment, a local newspaper said.

Cavallo told Jornal do Brasil in an exclusive interview that Brazil's macroeconomic picture today is like Argentina's in 1992 but that Brasilia needs to accelerate reforms and deregulation to avoid similar pitfalls.

"Our unemployment problem should be taken into account by Brazil so that, in two or three years because of delays in some key deregulations, you do not suffer unemployment problems," he was quoted as saying.
He cited specifically labor law reform, saying he regrets not having pushed through labor as well as health system reforms in Argentina in 1992.
But he added any similar changes in Brazilian legislation should be accompanied by job-creating measures.

Cavallo, a free-market economist who shepherded Argentina through seven years of austerity and deep structural reforms, was sacked earlier this year over policy differences with President Carlos Menem.
He was replaced as ecomony minister by Roque Fernandez, a former Central Bank chief.
Argentina in 1992 had 17.5 percent inflation but joblessness of six percent, he told the paper.
Brazil today has slashed inflation to an expected 13 percent for this year while unemployment ranges between an official 5.5 percent to as high as 15.5 percent, according to labor sources.
A controversial figure in Argentina, Cavallo denied he is considering running for president.
"I haven't thought about that subject yet," he said.
